items.title: Australia Aims to Make AI Labs Disclose Rogue Agents
items.summary: A new AI safety regulator would enforce the rules, though the government has yet to formally propose it. The Australian AI Safety Institute would back the regulator with technical help. Frontier labs would have to tell officials quickly when something goes wrong and let independent testers evaluate their models. The rules would further require developers to keep safeguards in place from the lab through live deployment and to make their safety and security policies public. The government has yet to set penalty amounts or release other details of the plan. Albanese told reporters, "Australia is a first mover in this space" and said existing law lags the technology in some areas.

items.title: EU Market Turns to Domestic Cybersecurity Tech
items.summary: According to figures released Wednesday by British market intelligence firm Context, the last two years saw a 35% rise in the sales of cybersecurity products from EU-headquartered vendors through distributors in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Sales from all vendors rose by 10% during that time while U.S. vendors saw only an 8% sales lift.

items.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
items.summary: German defense technology company Quantum Systems confirmed that it detected an incident in late October that was part of an active cyberattack by "hostile actors." Quantum Systems believes it was targeted because of its recent announcement of support for Ukraine and says it is working closely with state authorities to investigate the attack.

items.title: n8n: Custom Instance Role with User Management Permissions Gives Control of the Owner Account
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 7.5, CVEs: , Summary: n8n protected the instance owner account from changes by every other user. The password reset link and role change operations did not apply that protection to users with a custom instance role. A user whose custom instance role included user management permissions could obtain a password reset link for the owner and take over the owner account, or change the owner's role. This gave the attacker full control of the instance. items.title: Microsoft’s global outage may be worse than Amazon’s or CrowdStrike’s, expert says
items.summary: Similar to recent world-shaking outages of widely used tech like Amazon Web Services and CrowdStrike, the Microsoft disruption looks like “one of the biggest outages of all time,” Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre, told NBC News. Possibly even “worse,” he suggested.

items.title: German parliament passes law giving spy agencies hacking, sabotage powers
items.summary: German lawmakers passed legislation Friday allowing the country’s intelligence agencies to hack foreign systems, sabotage adversaries’ supply chains and take down servers run by hostile state-backed hackers. Rewriting the laws governing both Germany’s foreign intelligence service, the BND, and its domestic agency for the protection of the constitutional order, the BfV, the government bill gives the BND powers to act against threats abroad rather than simply report on them. The BfV gets a shorter list of covert powers inside Germany, such as blocking or rerouting data traffic, but it remains prohibited from using force against people — something which remains the sole prerogative of law enforcement in the country.

items.title: NATO issues and then withdraws Russian taxi app travel advice for defense industry conference
items.summary: NATO on Thursday issued and then withdrew guidance suggesting attendees of its flagship defense industry conference in Turkey use a Russian-owned taxi app, after concerns were raised that doing so could expose their movements and locations to Russian intelligence.
